grounded_in: CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v3.0 control numbering, reproduced from the publicly documented control catalog. Re-verify control numbers against the current CIS benchmark PDF before citing a version number to a user.
note: Each entry is the canonical metadata for one rule. scripts/audit_tf_gcp.py loads this file at runtime and only implements a check() function for entries where automated is true; automated:false entries are surfaced as manual-review items in the report because they require org-level or cross-resource context a single Terraform plan cannot see.

controls.title: Bucket grants access to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers
controls.rationale: Any IAM binding/member on a bucket (or its object ACLs) that names allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers makes the bucket's contents readable/writable by anyone on the internet, bypassing per-object ACL review entirely.
controls.remediation: Remove the allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers member from the binding. Set public_access_prevention = "enforced" on the google_storage_bucket resource so this cannot be reintroduced by a future object ACL change.

controls.title: Bucket does not enforce uniform bucket-level access
controls.rationale: Without uniform_bucket_level_access = true, individual objects can carry their own legacy ACLs that silently override the bucket-level IAM policy administrators believe is authoritative.
controls.remediation: Set uniform_bucket_level_access = true in the google_storage_bucket resource block.

controls.title: Ingress firewall rule opens SSH (22) or RDP (3389) from 0.0.0.0/0
controls.rationale: Management ports reachable from the entire internet are the single most common initial-access vector in GCP compromises; brute-force and credential-stuffing bots scan 0.0.0.0/0 continuously.
controls.remediation: Restrict source_ranges to known bastion/VPN CIDR ranges, or remove the rule and use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) TCP forwarding with a firewall rule scoped to 35.235.240.0/20 instead.

controls.title: Ingress firewall rule allows all protocols/ports from 0.0.0.0/0
controls.rationale: A rule with no protocol/port restriction and a public source range is a de facto 'allow all' rule regardless of what other, narrower rules exist alongside it.
controls.remediation: Scope the allow block to the specific protocol and port range the workload needs; never leave ports unset on a rule with a 0.0.0.0/0 source range.

controls.title: Subnetwork does not have VPC Flow Logs enabled
controls.rationale: Flow Logs are the primary forensic record for lateral-movement and exfiltration investigations; without them there is no network-layer audit trail once an incident is already in progress.
controls.remediation: Add a log_config block to the google_compute_subnetwork resource (aggregation_interval, flow_sampling, metadata).

controls.title: Primitive role (roles/owner, roles/editor) granted at project scope
controls.rationale: Primitive roles grant broad, undifferentiated permissions across every service in the project. A compromised principal with roles/editor can read secrets, exfiltrate data, and modify IAM policy itself.
controls.remediation: Replace with the narrowest predefined role(s) that cover the principal's actual needs (see references/iam_least_privilege_guidelines.md), or a custom role scoped to the exact permission set.

controls.title: User-managed service account key created
controls.rationale: Long-lived, downloadable service account keys are the most commonly leaked GCP credential (committed to repos, embedded in CI logs) and never expire unless manually rotated or revoked.
controls.remediation: Remove the google_service_account_key resource. Use Workload Identity Federation (GKE Workload Identity, or external Workload Identity Federation for non-GCP workloads) or short-lived impersonated credentials instead.

controls.title: Cloud SQL instance has a public IP (ipv4_enabled = true)
controls.rationale: A publicly routable Cloud SQL instance depends entirely on authorized-networks and password strength for protection, removing the network-layer isolation that private IP + VPC peering provides by default.
controls.remediation: Set ipv4_enabled = false in the ip_configuration block and connect via private_network (VPC peering) or the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy.

controls.title: Cloud SQL instance does not require SSL/TLS for connections
controls.rationale: Without require_ssl (or the newer ssl_mode requiring encrypted transport), client-to-instance traffic including credentials can be observed on any network path between them.
controls.remediation: Set require_ssl = true (or ssl_mode = "ENCRYPTED_ONLY"/"TRUSTED_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED" on providers that support it) in the ip_configuration block.

controls.title: Cloud SQL instance has automated backups disabled
controls.rationale: Without backup_configuration.enabled, there is no point-in-time recovery path for accidental deletion, ransomware, or a bad migration.
controls.remediation: Add a backup_configuration block with enabled = true and a point_in_time_recovery_enabled = true where the engine supports it.

controls.title: GKE cluster has legacy ABAC authorization enabled
controls.rationale: enable_legacy_abac = true re-enables the coarse, pre-RBAC authorization model GKE deprecated specifically because it cannot express least-privilege access to cluster resources.
controls.remediation: Remove enable_legacy_abac or set it to false; rely on Kubernetes RBAC (the GKE default) instead.

controls.title: GKE cluster is not configured as a private cluster
controls.rationale: Without a private_cluster_config block enabling private nodes, cluster nodes receive external IPs, directly exposing the kubelet and node OS to the internet.
controls.remediation: Add private_cluster_config { enable_private_nodes = true ... } and restrict control-plane access with master_authorized_networks_config.

controls.title: GKE cluster does not have Network Policy enabled
controls.rationale: Without network_policy.enabled, every pod can reach every other pod in the cluster by default, so a single compromised pod can pivot laterally without any firewalling.
controls.remediation: Add network_policy { enabled = true } (and enable the corresponding addon on the node pool's provider, e.g. Calico/Dataplane V2).

controls.title: KMS key has no rotation period, or one longer than 90 days
controls.rationale: A key that is never rotated has an ever-growing blast radius: every object ever encrypted with it remains exposed for as long as that one key material is valid.
controls.remediation: Set rotation_period to "7776000s" (90 days) or less on the google_kms_crypto_key resource.

controls.title: BigQuery dataset grants access to allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers
controls.rationale: An access block special_group or iam_member naming allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers makes every table in the dataset queryable by anyone with a Google account or, in the allUsers case, anyone at all.
controls.remediation: Remove the allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers entry from the access block; grant named principals or groups the narrowest predefined BigQuery role that covers their need.

controls.title: Compute instance has serial port access enabled
controls.rationale: metadata["serial-port-enable"] = "true" exposes an interactive console over the network to anyone with the right IAM permission, bypassing SSH key and OS Login controls entirely.
controls.remediation: Remove the serial-port-enable metadata key, or set it to "false" explicitly.

controls.title: Project-level Cloud Audit Logging or an aggregated log sink is not configured
controls.rationale: Without Data Access audit logs and a durable, access-controlled log sink, there is no tamper-resistant record of who accessed what, which is usually the deciding evidence in an incident review.
controls.remediation: Configure google_project_iam_audit_config for the services in scope, and a google_logging_project_sink routing logs to a dedicated, access-restricted project or bucket. This requires organization-level context this scanner cannot fully verify from one module's plan -- confirm manually.

controls.title: Org policy constraints for public access prevention / external IPs / SA keys are not enforced
controls.rationale: Resource-level fixes (e.g. public_access_prevention on one bucket) can be silently undone by the next commit unless an org policy constraint makes the secure state the default for every future resource.
controls.remediation: Enforce constraints/storage.publicAccessPrevention, constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess, and constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation at the folder or org level. Verify manually -- these constraints usually live outside the module being scanned.
